build.provenance: explicit orchestrator build configuration; throughput is not a release-profile claim

work_conserving_assertions.scope: logical scheduler reservations at deterministic arrival/release events; CPU execution measured separately

scopes.pool: exact logical scheduler release events, actual WorkerPool occupied time, logical charged peaks and scheduler queue wait
scopes.http: real API/worker/object-store TCP, serial result oracles, accepted-ID conservation, client latency and receipt queue-wait bounds
scopes.sampled: persisted heartbeat CPU/byte reservations and OS RSS/CPU, with configured 250ms sample/publication intervals
scopes.queue_payloads: actual successful signed Record wire request/pin/result bytes; excludes allocator metadata and unobserved local transitions

limitations: unoptimized dev profile, not release throughput
local conditional SQLite storage, not AWS S3 or a cloud provider benchmark
heartbeat samples do not prove continuous HTTP compute occupancy
HTTP server queue wait is bounded by receipt observations; exact scheduler wait is measured in the pool benchmark
postprocessing: Only Matplotlib label compatibility changed after measurement; runtime/workload/configuration/oracles are unchanged.

methods.queue_payload_scope: successful signed Record payload bytes; excludes allocator metadata and unobserved local transitions
methods.network_scope: protocol bytes counted once per proxied RPC, including HTTP headers; excludes TCP/IP headers and retransmission counters
methods.pool_wait_scope: request arrival to job closure start; mixed socket jobs include their precompute IO stage
methods.http_queue_wait_scope: receipt-state observation bounds including ingress, at 100ms polling
